behavioral_notes.observation: When the ordered product is type='service' with service_type='timesheet', qty_delivered_method is set to 'timesheet'; qty_delivered is then computed NOT from stock moves but by summing logged hours: _get_delivered_quantity_by_analytic over account.analytic.line where project_id is set. This is the core monetization step - delivered effort (hours) becomes the billable delivered quantity on the sales line. Formula lives in Python, invisible to metadata.

Each timesheet line (account.analytic.line with a project) is auto-linked to a sale.order.line via so_line, resolved by the project's pricing_type: task_rate -> task's sale_line_id; fixed_rate -> project's sale_line_id; employee_rate -> the project.sale.line.employee.map entry matching the employee (else falls back to task/project SOL). This is the project/task<->sale linkage that routes each hour to the right billable line and unit price. so_line is editable (is_so_line_edited) and skipped once invoiced.

Invoice-on-delivered-hours: for service_type='timesheet' / invoice_policy='delivery' lines, draft invoice creation searches timesheets in the period and stamps timesheet_invoice_id = the invoice line's move, marking those hours invoiced; qty_to_invoice is recomputed from not-yet-invoiced timesheets. action_post on a credit note (out_refund) un-stamps timesheet_invoice_id so the hours become re-billable. Closes the deliver->invoice loop of the value-shop.

Each timesheet is classified billable_time / timesheet_revenues / billable_fixed / billable_milestones / billable_manual / non_billable from its so_line product policy, and the project profitability panel aggregates analytic-line cost (negative amount) vs revenue (positive) per type - turning logged effort into a live cost/revenue/margin view of the engagement.

Ships a master data product 'Service on Timesheets' (type=service, service_policy=delivered_timesheet, uom=hour, list_price 40) used as the default project timesheet_product_id; it is protected from archive/delete/company-link. _is_delivered_timesheet() gates the timesheet billing path. This is the concrete value-shop product definition (type=service + timesheet) from VALUE_MODELS_THREE_AR.

1 JS file + 1 XML template: OWL component SoLineField registered as fields:so_line_field, also pushed into the project.webclient bundle, letting timesheet grids pick/show the sales order item (so_line) per line.

classification.rationale: sale_timesheet is the BRIDGE that monetizes the value-shop: it is the seam between the shop side (project/hr_timesheet, where unique customer problems are solved through cyclical logged effort) and the chain/cash side (sale, account). Concretely it turns hr_timesheet delivered effort into sale.order.line.qty_delivered (service_type='timesheet' => qty_delivered computed from logged hours via _get_delivered_quantity_by_analytic), auto-routes each hour to the right billable line/unit-price via project pricing_type (task/fixed/employee rate) and the project.sale.line.employee.map, then invoices on delivered hours (timesheet_invoice_id stamping) and reports revenue/margin - realizing the value-shop revenue where value is known by delivered effort. It depends on sale_project + hr_timesheet and auto-installs, so it exists only as the connective tissue. Value-shop primary activities per Stabell & Fjeldstad ('Execution' = hr_timesheet delivered work; monetized here); APQC 5.0 Deliver Services covers the deliver-and-bill-services flow. activity_class primary: it is on the revenue-producing service-delivery path, not a back-office support function.

standard_capabilities: delivered-timesheet service policy (qty_delivered from logged hours)

custom revenue-recognition / WIP accounting on unbilled hours
